title: Longer Contiguous Segments of Ones than Zeros
spaceBreakdown:
- int max1, max0, run, i: scalars → O(1)
- not counted: input string s
approach: Scan the string once, tracking the current run of identical characters. When the character changes (or the string ends), record the run length into `max1` or `max0` depending on the character, then reset the run counter. At the end, return whether `max1 > max0`. This is correct because every maximal contiguous segment is finalized exactly once-either when the next character differs or at the end of the string.
hints: As you scan the string left to right, when does the count of consecutive identical characters need to be recorded, and when does it simply grow by one?
Single pass with run-length tracking. In `"1101"`, the first two `'1'`s form a run of length 2; when `'0'` appears, record that run of 2 ones and start counting zeros.

**Single character** - string has length 1, so the run counter starts and ends at 1
`Input: s = "1"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: initializing `run` to 0 instead of 1 → `max1 = max(0, 0) = 0`, returns false

**Last run skipped** - the final run of identical characters is never finalized if updates only happen on character change
`Input: s = "0111"` → `Expected: true`
⚠️ Bug: updating `max1`/`max0` only inside the "character changed" branch with no post-loop update → `max1` stays 0, returns false

**Tie** - longest run of ones equals longest run of zeros
`Input: s = "111000"` → `Expected: false`
⚠️ Bug: using `>=` instead of `>` in the return statement → returns true

followUps.q: If the string arrives as an infinite stream and you must answer "is the longest 1-run strictly longer than the longest 0-run so far?" at any time, how would you adapt?
followUps.a: Keep `max1`, `max0`, the current run length, and the current character. Each incoming character either extends the current run or finalizes it (updating `max1` or `max0`) and starts a new run of length 1. Answer `max1 > max0` on demand. TC O(1) per character, SC O(1).

followUps.q: What if you must return true only when every 1-run is strictly longer than every 0-run adjacent to it?
followUps.a: Collect runs as (char, length) pairs in one pass, then check each 1-run against its immediate neighboring 0-runs. TC O(n), SC O(n) for the run list (reducible to O(1) if you only keep the last two runs and stream-check).

followUps.q: What if the string has up to 10^9 characters but is given as run-length encoded pairs (char, count)?
followUps.a: Iterate through the pairs directly, updating `max1` and `max0` from the counts without expanding. TC O(k) where k is the number of runs, SC O(1).
